title: The Heartbreaking Mistake Sellers Make Before It’s Too Late

content.text: There are a few things that I see people do wrong that really break my heart when it comes to selling their business. I'm Sarah Sharp. I'm a deal attorney. I help people buy and sell businesses every day. And I specifically help people in the accounting practice industry. And this week, I've had a trend where I have met with a number of sellers who were not intending to sell, but there was an unfortunate life event where they had to. And in that instance, one of those happened. And I had another deal where they had just gone under LOI. But unfortunately, one of the owners had come down with a terminal diagnosis and that put the entire sale for all of the other owners in jeopardy and probably meant that instead of selling, they're looking at having a 3 or 4 year stabilization process before they will even be able to have a firm that they can sell. That is not ideal. And there's not ever I don't think anyone who's going to tell you that you shouldn't be doing succession planning from day one. But seeing it and going through it with clients really hammers it home. So I just want to tell you about the cycle of a sale.
